question.text: This was the largest boat of the three in Columbus's fleet. It ran aground due to incompetent piloting and was dismantled to build the first Spanish settlement in the New World.
question.clue: This ship, the largest and slowest of the three that Christopher Columbus used in his first voyage to the Americas.

swap.leadin: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa paved the way for successful later sieges of Cordoba and Seville in this conflict.
swap.text: Name this religious conflict between Christian states and Muslim states in the Iberian Peninsula, which is named for the reacquisition of traditionally Christian lands.
swap.clue: During this period, a coalition of Christian knights joined together to defeat Muhammad al-Nasir at the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa.

question.leadin: This group was commanded by the Duke of Medina Sidonia after its initially designated leader, Alvaro de Bazan, died.
question.text: Name this massive naval fleet whose intended invasion of England failed.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Invincible Armada or Armada Invencible]
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.leadin: This empire's former colony of St. Augustine is considered the oldest city in the present-day U.S.
swap.text: Name this empire, whose explorer Alonso Alvarez de Pineda created the first known map depicting Texas.
swap.clue: The Abraham Lincoln Brigade was a group of American volunteers who fought in this country, which was also the site of the Nazi-sponsored Condor Legion's most infamous atrocity.

question.leadin: This war was supposed to be avoided through the First and Second Partition Treaties.
question.text: Name this 13-year conflict over control of an Iberian nation. It was sparked by the death of the childless King Charles II.
question.clue: The North American theater of this conflict was known as Queen Anne's War.

swap.leadin: It was ruled by the Nasrid dynasty before its 1492 capture.
swap.text: Name this last Moorish outpost in southern Spain which contained the Alhambra.
swap.clue: Following his honeymoon with Isabella of Portugal, Charles V had a palace constructed by Diego Machuca within the walls of this city's most famous structure.

question.text: Unsurprisingly, Salazar was a big fan of this longtime dictator of Spain, who ruled from 1939 to 1975. His party was known as the Falange, and he was supported by the Carlists.
question.clue: That 1959 Stabilization Plan, advocated by members of Opus Dei, ended this leader's autarkic economic policies.

swap.text: During Franco's regime, he allowed the German Condor Legion to follow through with the bombing of this Basque town.
swap.clue: The Spanish Civil War of 1936-9, a victory for Francisco Franco's Falange fascist forces over the Republicans, is often considered a "trial run" or proxy for World War II. It was characterized by atrocities on both sides, including the bombing of this Basque town by the Condor Legion of the Luftwaffe, an event commemorated by Picasso.

question.leadin: Some people investigated by this body were forced to wear a conical hat called a coroza, while others were given a garment known as a sanbenito.
question.text: Name this body established in Spain by Ferdinand and Isabella. It routed out "insincere" conversos.
question.clue: Officially declared by Sixtus IV in 1478, it was overseen by the Consejo Supremo, while Miguel de Morillo and Juan de San Martin oversaw it in Seville.

swap.text: The Roman legion was proven superior over the Greek phalanx at the 197 BCE Battle of Cynoscephalae when forces under Titus Quinctius Flamininus defeated those commanded by this monarch.
swap.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

question.text: This 1212 battle was a huge defeat for the Almohads in Andalusia at the hands of various Christian Iberian kingdoms. It set in motion a process that, by the end of the century, reduced Muslim presence in Spain to basically just Granada.
question.answer: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
question.clue: Innocent III convinced some veterans of the Fourth Crusade to campaign with the winning side in this battle, whose commanders included Sancho VII of Navarre.

swap.text: This daughter of Ferdinand and Isabella and wife of Phillip the Handsome was a Queen of Spain who suffered from mental illness and was forced to live in a nunnery for much of her reign.
swap.answerHtml: Joanna the Mad [or Juana la Loca; or Joanna of Castile; or Juana de Castilla]
swap.clue: After Charles was elected Holy Roman Emperor, the Comuneros rebellion in Spain tried to overthrow him in favor of this woman, his mother, who was confined for her alleged mental illness after the revolt was put down.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Confederacion Nacional del Trabajo ("trah-BAH-hoh"), or CNT.
question.text: The CNT was founded following a 1910 workers' congress in this city. A 1909 general strike resulted in the "Tragic Week" in this capital of Catalonia.
question.clue: A rebellion in this city erupted on July 19, 1936 when news of a coup launched by the military against the government of Manuel Azana reached it, with the result that the rebels captured the San Andres and Atarazanas barracks.

swap.leadin: This communist activist, who was nicknamed after a flower, proclaimed that "they shall not pass" while Madrid was under siege.
swap.text: Name this longtime leader of the Communist Party of Spain in exile. She was elected to the Spanish parliament in 1977 following the restoration of democracy.

question.leadin: This campaign was legendarily brought on after a king opened 27 padlocks to enter a chamber and read a scroll, which prophesied that the horsemen painted on the walls would invade his kingdom.
question.text: Describe this campaign that began with the defeat of King Roderic at an early 8th-century AD battle that was won by a Berber general.
question.answerHtml: the Arab conquest of Spain [accept answers with Umayyad or Muslim or Tariq ibn Ziyad in place of “Arab”; accept the fall of the Visigothic Kingdom or clear equivalents; accept answers with synonyms for conquest or fall; accept the Battle of Guadalete or the Battle of 711; accept answers with Iberia or Hispania or Andalusia or al-Andalus or the Visigothic Kingdom in place of “Spain”]

swap.leadin: This man led Spanish troops to force Portugal to cease trade with Britain as part of a Franco-Spanish alliance in the brief War of the Oranges.
swap.text: Name this "Prince of the Peace", a powerful prime minister under Charles IV.
swap.clue: He became his country's first commander to adopt the title of generalisimo while leading troops in the War of the Oranges.

question.text: In a later campaign, the Black Prince defeated Henry of Trastamara at this 1367 battle named for a small Spanish town, fighting on behalf of Peter the Cruel during the Civil War of Castile.
question.clue: This 1367 battle of Castilian civil war that saw Pedro the Cruel emerge victorious over his half-brother Henry of Trastamara. Notable allies of the victorious side included John of Gaunt and another English leader.

swap.leadin: This kingdom was formed after a revolt led by the Pamplonan king Inigo Arista against the local Franks.
swap.text: Name this kingdom, whose most famous and final ruler was Henry III, who was killed by Francois Ravaillac as King of France after saying "Paris is well worth a mass" and issuing the Edict of Nantes.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a certain diplomat, FTPE.
question.text: The Cortes at Cadiz first appointed him as an ambassador, but it was not until Ferdinand VII was restored to power that the U.S. would receive him for negotiations.

swap.leadin: The Onacino and Gamboino clans fought during this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict in medieval Spain between landowners called juanchos in which many dorretxeak were built.
swap.answerHtml: The War of the Bands [accept Guerra de los Bandos; accept Bando Gerrak]
